title: 1997 AHSME Problem 14
statement: The number of geese in a flock increases so that the difference between the populations in year \(n+2\) and year \(n\) is directly proportional to the population in year \(n+1.\) If the populations in the years \(1994,\) \(1995,\) and \(1997\) were \(39,\) \(60,\) and \(123,\) respectively, then the population in \(1996\) was

solutions.text: The rule gives \(x-39=60k\) and \(123-60=kx.\) Eliminating \(k\) yields \(x(x-39)=3780,\) or \((x-84)(x+45)=0.\) The population is positive, so \(x=84,\) and B is correct.
hints: Let \(x\) be the \(1996\) population and \(k\) the constant of proportionality
Translate the years \(1994\)–\(1996\) and \(1995\)–\(1997\) into two equations using the same \(k\)
